text:
elena: Heads-up — customer reported they revoked a BYOK master key in their HSM and now our KMS proxy is returning 403 for decrypt requests. Can ops confirm propagation window and who needs RBAC lifted/changed on our side?
ben: are we seeing errors in the decrypt path only or auth failures for key access too?
carla: saw a spike of `kms.proxy: permission_denied` in logs a few mins ago. I pulled a sample: `request_id=6f2b4, status=403, error=key_revoked`
frank: devops-bot opened INC-1123 for this automatically when the alert hit. @elena can you confirm customer rotated vs revoked? rotate should still allow rewraps if we have current wrapped key. revoke is full deny.
devops-bot: Incident INC-1123 created: oncall=frank, sev=2, owner=eng-security. Link: https://incidents.example/INC-1123 :warning:
sasha: customer says they performed a 'destructive revoke' in their HSM console — they explicitly zeroed the key material. That sounds like full custody break.
elena: correct — they used their HSM operator flow to revoke. They want assurance we won't have any remaining plaintext or wrapped key artifacts. Compliance asked for proof of deletion.
carla: two questions: 1) do we cache any unwrapped key material anywhere? 2) do we store wrapped key blobs that we could still use to rewrap if customer rotates?
frank: short answers: 1) no persistent plaintext caching in prod runtime — only transient in process memory. 2) we persist wrapped key blobs for customers that opted into rewrap service, but access requires our KMS to call the customer's HSM for unwrap or an HSM-backed rewrap token.
ben: the problem is RBAC on our side — our service account still has permission to call the customer's KMS proxy. If the customer revoked the master key, any future unwraps should fail but we need to confirm we aren't able to reconstitute older wrapped blobs.
elena: security needs an audit trail for SOC2 and ISO — timestamps, operator identity from HSM attestation, and proof we attempted decrypt and got denied. Can someone run a query across SIEM for that request_id and for `key_revoked` events across last 24h?
carla: on it. sample SIEM query I'm going to run:
```
index=prod_kms_logs "key_revoked" OR "permission_denied" | stats count by event_type, source, customer_id
```
carla: also checking for any anomalies where `unwrap` succeeded after revoke.
sasha: we should also validate HSM attestation statements — customer can provide an ATE (attestation) or we can request signed `key-state` metadata from their HSM gateway. That helps compliance.
frank: incident response note — if a customer does destructive revoke, we must: 1) mark customer data as inaccessible, 2) stop scheduled rewrap jobs, 3) notify product and sales, 4) produce audit packet. I'll update the runbook.
elena: RBAC question: do we need to remove the service account entitlement immediately or can we block at proxy gate? What's the minimal blast radius for other customers?
ben: prefer blocking by customer_id at proxy layer — less risk. But we also need a short-lived RBAC revocation for the service account token so re-issuance won't happen while we investigate.
carla: implemented temporary rule in proxy: `block(customer_id=acme-co, action=unwrap)` — I've pushed a canary rule to staging and will rollout to prod after 2m smoke.
frank: make sure audit logs capture the proxy rule change and who made it. We need entries: "rule_change", old_value, new_value, actor.
sec-bot: Audit entry recorded: actor=carla, action=proxy_rule_update, target=acme-co, timestamp=2102345702
elena: excellent. For compliance packet — we need: HSM attestation, SIEM logs for attempted unwraps, proxy rule change audit, and a signed statement from us confirming we hold no plaintext and that wrapped blobs cannot be decrypted. Who will draft the statement?
sasha: I can draft an attestation template and ask for legal review. Will include the memory handling guarantees and rewrap policy references.
ben: vuln-triage note — this suggests a gap in our incident flow: we didn't have an automatic hold on rewrap jobs when receiving `key_revoked`. Add a detector to the KMS proxy that flips a feature flag per-customer to stop rewraps.
frank: filed ENG-4987 to add that detector and a playbook task to automatically create an audit packet. Priorities: P1 for incidents involving destructive revokes.
elena: action items: Carla — push proxy block to prod and send audit IDs; Sasha — draft attestation and loop in legal; Ben — implement KMS-proxy detector (eng ticket exists); Frank — own incident comms and prod rollback plan. Please post updates here.
carla: proxy block live in prod at 2102345705. Audit IDs: proxy_change=aud-5541, block_rule=aud-5542.
sasha: attestation draft in Google Drive: https://drive.example/attest/ACME-revoke-draft.docx — looping legal (legal@redwood).
ben: ENG-4987 created and assigned to me, ETA EOD tomorrow.
frank: comms draft for customer and SOC2 auditors in INC-1123 notes. I'll attach SIEM extracts once Carla posts them.
elena: thanks all. One last ask — security wants a signed, time-bound evidence package that includes a hash of wrapped blobs we have (so customer can verify we didn't alter anything) and the statement we couldn't decrypt after revoke. Can we produce those hashes?
carla: yes — I can export the per-blob SHA256 hashes and include them in the packet. Will redact blob content.
sec-bot: Evidence package queued: package_id=EP-210234-1, includes: HSM_attestation_placeholder, SIEM_extracts, hash_manifest, proxy_audit.
elena: closing loop — we'll run a short tabletop to update the runbook for destructive revokes next week. Marking this thread for post-incident review. :white_check_mark:
